source.title: Moderate similarity leads to empathic concern, but high similarity can also induce personal distress towards others' pain.

confidence_rationale: The named L3 anchor for the loveability_coupling_gain UPPER BOUND. Experimentally manipulating perceived self-other similarity (low/moderate/high) toward an injured target: moderate similarity yielded empathic concern WITHOUT personal distress (reduced disgust/avoidance), while high similarity produced empathic concern but ALSO as much personal-distress signalling as the low-similarity group -- a non-monotone, inverted-U relationship. This is the direct empirical basis for INV-082's claim that loveability/coupling is bounded ('care internalised as personally-applicable AND stable', not 'more coupling is better') and for the DEV-NEED-017 loveability_coupling_gain ceiling. Held at 0.6 by a single modest-N lab study (n=87), indirect self-other-distress measures (facial disgust as a personal-distress proxy), and the gap from inter-personal empathy similarity to an intra-agent self-valence coupling parameter.
failure_signatures: Single study, n=87, with personal distress operationalised indirectly (facial disgust / avoidance, gaze, pupil) rather than by a validated distress instrument -- the inversion at high similarity is suggestive, not a precisely-located threshold; it does NOT license the specific [0.1, 0.7] numeric bound, only the qualitative claim that an upper bound exists.

The coupling here is BETWEEN two people (observer vs injured target); INV-082's loveability_coupling_gain is a within-agent coupling of received care into self-valence -- the inverted-U may not transfer cleanly across that reframing, and the high-similarity 'personal distress' failure mode is an analogy for over-coupling, not a measurement of it.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Perceived similarity to a suffering target has a non-monotone effect on vicarious emotion: moderate similarity maximises empathic concern while minimising personal distress (less avoidance/disgust), but high similarity, although it raises empathic concern, also raises personal distress to the level of the low-similarity condition. Empathy is optimised at intermediate, not maximal, self-other overlap.
mapping.ree_translation: INV-082 explicitly asserts a BOUNDED loveability ('Salles 2024, bounded') -- care must be internalised as personally-applicable but the coupling has an upper limit above which it inverts into the personal-distress failure (the adult analogue of MECH-158 'love exists but not for me', here 'the other's pain becomes my own distress'). The plan's DEV-NEED-017 readout pins loveability_coupling_gain to [0.1, 0.7] with the upper bound credited to this paper: over-coupling is the failure, not the goal. Salles et al. supply the empirical inverted-U that makes the upper bound load-bearing rather than a free parameter, and is the standing guard against any 'more coupling is better' design of LOVE-2.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper measures interpersonal empathy as a function of observer-target similarity; INV-082's coupling is a within-agent term (received care -> self-valence). The transfer is by structural analogy (a coupling strength with an inverted-U optimum), and the study does NOT validate the specific numeric interval [0.1, 0.7] -- it supports only the QUALITATIVE existence of an upper bound. Personal distress is measured by indirect behavioural proxies (facial disgust, avoidance) in a single n=87 sample.
mapping.source_context: 87 adult participants; video of an athlete in pain preceded by a similarity-priming clip (low/moderate/high); emotional self-reports, facial action coding, gaze, and pupillometry.

confidence_components.notes: Modest single-study evidence with indirect distress measures -> moderate source quality. Mapping fidelity moderate: the inverted-U is the right SHAPE for INV-082's bounded coupling, but it is interpersonal-empathy similarity, not within-agent self-valence coupling, and it does not pin the numeric bound. This entry grounds the BOUND qualitatively; the [0.1,0.7] interval remains a design choice, not a measured threshold.
